youtube.title: How One Pore Turns Into a Pimple | Skin Sense No. 016
youtube.caption:
A pimple begins deep inside a pore, long before you see anything.

Oil and cells pack into a tiny plug… and the doorway starts to close. Immune cells gather, and the spot turns red, warm, and swollen.

Series: Season 1: The organ you live inside, part 16 of 6.

Sources
1. Acne lesions begin as a microcomedone, a microscopic plug in the follicle, before anything is visible. — NCBI (NIH): https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK459173
2. Sebum and keratinous debris form a plug in the follicle; the lesion is open or closed depending on whether the orifice stays patent. — statpearls.com: https://statpearls.com/sp/al/9/17101/
3. An open comedone's dark color comes from oxidation of lipids and melanin in the plug exposed to air, not from dirt. — NIH: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10939092
4. A closed comedone (whitehead) stays skin-coloured or pale because the plug is covered by a thin layer of epithelium. — my.clevelandclinic.org: https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/comedonal-acne
5. Immune cells (neutrophils, lymphocytes) are recruited and the lesion becomes inflamed (redness, warmth, swelling). — frontiersin.org: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2024.1275269

Illustrations: AI-generated and 3-D animation made in code, no stock footage. Narration: a real person's voice (recorded, not AI). Cover illustration made with AI. Every number is checked against the sources.

Skin Sense: Skin biology, ingredients and routines, with the evidence on the screen.
